verdicts.why: Steering a course somewhere (head north, head home) states direction and takes no side on it.
Being first in a class or list is a rank; the standing is the meaning, and the word adds no admiration beyond stating it.
A name that heads a list or a title that heads a page is a plain statement of position.
A cabbage or a boil coming to a head is botanical or bodily description with no attitude.
A river heading in the hills is geographic fact, not opinion.
Heading a fish or a stalk names the act plainly; an unpleasant referent is not a loaded word.
Where 'promise' means to foretell (it promises rain, promises to be a long night) it states an expectation and can run good or bad, so the word itself takes no side.
A way of regarding a topic is named without judging the regard; 'view' is the plain neighbour, not a loaded one.
As a personal belief it is the neutral word for an opinion, carrying neither the dismissal of 'notion' nor the weight of 'conviction'.
A stated opinion is named flatly; the word says nothing about whether the opinion is sound or foolish.
The act of seeing something (in view, within view) is bare description.
Outward appearance named as 'view' carries no approval or contempt for what is seen.
A prospect or aim in view (with a view to, views of domestic happiness) is named without judging it.
A picture of a scene is a plain object name.
A formal accusation laid before a court is a legal term of art; the crime is unpleasant but the word is neutral.
A technical measure in communication theory cannot carry attitude.
To intend a meaning by a word (what do you intend by that?) is plain description of signifying.
Relating to nature (natural science, natural causes) describes a domain and does not praise or blame.
Calling someone a natural at something asserts inborn talent, and that assertion is the meaning itself rather than an attitude layered over it, much as 'huge' is not 'monstrous'.
An instinctive reaction (a cat's natural aversion to water) is described, not judged; 'unthinking' in the gloss means unreflective, not careless.
Neither supernatural nor magical is a plain classification of what exists in the observable world.
Related by blood (natural parent, natural child) as glossed is a statement of kinship, not an appraisal of the person.
Natural rubber, natural gas and natural fibre are plainly unprocessed; the wholesome halo in food marketing comes from valuing the referent, not from the word.
A note that is neither sharp nor flat is pure music notation.
Money available to borrow is a banking term with no side taken.
A film or book credit is an entry on a list, described flatly.
A source note is a plain bibliographic object.
A course credit is an administrative unit and carries no attitude.
An estimate of creditworthiness names a financial standing, which may be good or bad, without the word judging it.
An accounting entry is bookkeeping vocabulary with no evaluative load.
